newsitem.title: USA: ComEd Ill. nuke returns to full power.
newsitem.headline: ComEd Ill. nuke returns to full power.

text.p: Commonwealth Edison Co's 789 megawatt (MW) Quad Cities nuclear power unit 2 returned to full power over the weekend from a repair outage that began Oct 24, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said.
The Cordova, Ill., unit was operating at 100 percent of capacity as of early Monday morning, according to the NRC's daily plant status report.
Quad Cities 2 was taken off line due to a problem with a steam turbine valve.
Also, Quad Cities unit 1 reduced power over the weekend while ComEd completed work on reactor feed pump seals, the NRC said in the status report.
The unit, also located at Cordova with a capacity of 789 MW, was operating at 52 percent of capacity as of early Monday, the NRC said.
Quad Cities 1 had been operating at 100 percent output last Friday, the NRC said.
A company spokesman was not immediately available to comment on when unit 1 would return to full power.
Commonwealth Edison is a subsidiary of Unicom Corp.
